instructions: The day before, or up to 2 days ahead: rinse the 1 cup jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 1 1/2 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Spread the rice on a plate or tray to cool, then cover and refrigerate. Cold, dry rice is what fries well, so don't use it warm.
Cut the pork tenderloin into 3/4-inch cubes. Sprinkle 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper over them and toss.

In a small bowl, stir together 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp sesame oil. Dice the red bell pepper, mince the 3 garlic cloves, mince 1 tbsp of ginger and slice the green onions, keeping the white and green parts apart. Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers.

Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in your largest wok or skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add the pork in a single layer and leave it alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is browned. Stir and cook for 3 minutes, until browned all over. Transfer it to a bowl.
You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a larger piece. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when it's just barely pink or white all the way through.

Add 1/2 tbsp of the oil to the pan, then the bell pepper and the frozen peas and carrots straight from the bag. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring now and then, for 5 minutes, until the pepper has softened and the peas and carrots are hot. Transfer them to the bowl with the pork.
Take the pan off the heat and add the last 1/2 tbsp oil, then the garlic, the ginger and the white parts of the green onions. Stir for 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the butter and the rice. Put the pan back on medium-high heat and stir, pressing the rice against the pan, for 3 minutes, until it's hot and the grains look separate and dry.
Push the rice to one side. Crack the 3 eggs into the empty space and scramble them for about 1 minute, until nearly set. Stir them into the rice.
Add the pork and vegetables with any juices from the bowl, the sauce and the green parts of the green onions. Toss for 1 minute, until everything is coated and hot. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve it hot, straight from the pan. For lunches, divide the rest into containers once it's cooled. It keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat in the microwave for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, stirring halfway.
advance_prep_notes: Cook and chill the rice a day ahead
method_notes: The lead is Well Plated's Pork Fried Rice (4.91 from 64 ratings, taken from the JSON-LD). Easy Peasy Foodie uses diced leftover pork, peas and sesame oil in a much shorter method, and The Kitchn and Eating on a Dime were blocked (403) so were not read. The sources agree on cold cooked rice, a hot wide pan, eggs scrambled in a cleared space and a soy and oyster sauce. This follows Well Plated: tenderloin browned first, vegetables next, then ginger and garlic off the heat, butter for the rice, and the sauce at the end. It uses 1 bell pepper and 1 bag of frozen peas and carrots for 4, and the rice is cooked a day ahead so the dish works as leftover-rice fried rice.
